what: Provenance of the experimental foot-model comparison and the D'Hondt port (FOOT_MODELS.md). None of the external files is in this repository; fetch them from the sources below and check these sha256 values.

saved_function.evaluated_with: casadi 3.8.2 (the file was saved by the paper's CasADi 3.5.5 code)

port.deterministic: two runs gave identical files (OpenSim 4.6, Python 3.13.16)

geometry_digest.computed_as: sha256 over the Geometry/*.stl files sorted by name: for each, its file name (UTF-8) then its sha256 as lowercase hex

two_segment.model: the pipeline's self-test output, opensim/model_scaled.osim (python -m rehabtwin selftest <dir>; synthetic squat)
two_segment.reproduced: pipeline/ and schemas/ of this repository at pipeline_commit, with Pose2Sim at the upstream commit below, gave this file byte for byte on the machine that recorded it (python -m rehabtwin selftest; checked 2026-11-04, OpenSim 4.6, numpy 2.5.4). The file depends on the machine. OpenBLAS's CPU-specific kernel is one cause (kernel tests on both machines below); a second, not identified, remains, since the laptop's kernel forced on the recording machine gives a third file. Only fitted marker positions and the last digit of muscle lengths differ in any case compared. On one machine it is the same on every build. The current pipeline gives the same geometry, joints and contact spheres but different body masses and inertias (about 3 % heavier), so it is not this model. workstation/setup.sh builds it from pipeline_commit and reports a sha256 other than this one without stopping; whether the comparison's results match results_2026-11-04.json is what counts.

kernel_test_on_the_recording_machine.machine: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz (AVX-512; numpy finds X86_V4), Ubuntu with glibc 2.39
kernel_test_on_the_recording_machine.haswell: with OPENBLAS_CORETYPE=Haswell: 794d669f543aded3938f9a95136dd447312af23bf61495ba7ab2c929be367866, the same on two builds, with numpy's AVX-512 paths disabled (NPY_DISABLE_CPU_FEATURES) and with one thread
kernel_test_on_the_recording_machine.against_recorded: 105 marker locations differ (up to 0.77 mm) and 28 optimal fibre and tendon slack lengths by at most 2.2e-16 m; body masses, inertias, geometry, joints and contact spheres are identical
kernel_test_on_the_recording_machine.conclusion: the OpenBLAS kernel changes the file, but the laptop's Haswell build (e0898ca7...) differs from this one, so a further machine difference (not threads, not numpy's own SIMD dispatch) also changes it; not identified

rebuilt_elsewhere.machine: Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra 9 290HX Plus (no AVX-512; OpenBLAS kernel Haswell), Ubuntu 26.04.1
rebuilt_elsewhere.same_on: three builds: workstation/setup.sh, a second build, and one with OMP_NUM_THREADS, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS and MKL_NUM_THREADS set to 1
rebuilt_elsewhere.kernel_test: with OPENBLAS_CORETYPE=Sandybridge the same machine gives 1238112f550d8024b41e58d32f30c11888ca613b619bfc3f04a284fa7ab83b4f. Against the Haswell build, 105 marker locations differ (up to 0.79 mm) and 41 muscle fibre and tendon lengths by at most 2.2e-16 m; body masses, inertias, geometry, joints and contact spheres are identical
rebuilt_elsewhere.comparison: workstation/run_comparison.sh with this model: all 244 result rows equal results_2026-11-04.json in every field except seconds

upstream.use: the self-test's base model and marker set (pipeline/configs/skel105_pose2sim.json); no hashes recorded

soles.other spacings made with: python sole_sim.py export out/sole_EU42_<side>.board.json --map maps/EU42_<side>_<hash>.json --spacing <mm> (generator commit 0257862; design hashes 636645a928..., 40fe8e1d0c...). Regenerating the EU 42 R board on 2026-11-04 and exporting it at 15 and 5 mm reproduced these files byte for byte

fetch: workstation/fetch_inputs.py fetches every external file above at its pinned commit and checks these hashes
